findings.basis: Re-read of round 60, ruled in rule round 61, item 1. Read 76ac4b69f950 listed these 37 profiles. Each rests on one maker or one file, with lineageos_device_overlays as its only recorded family, and together they reach 98 bundles. Motorola, 24 profiles and 78 bundles: TELUS plain 302-220 (53 bundles, one sdm632 block dated 2020-11-22), 310-000 by SPN, C Spire 311-230 and 311-630, Boost 311-870, 312-230, 312-280, 312-290, 312-430, 312-720 and 313-010 to 313-050. Sony, 5 profiles and 9 bundles: Airtel 404-45 and 404-90, Reliance 405-22, Jio 405-861 and 405-874. MediaTek's file, 8 profiles and 11 bundles: Orange MD 259-01, O2 262-11, Orange LU 270-99, Telekom MK 294-01, Telekom ME 297-02, SPM 308-03, Orange Caraibe 340-01 and Orange Reunion 647-00. No source says false, and no Google entry or operator statement speaks for the value on these networks: Google leaves the key unset or has no rule. OCD holds no operator statement on RTT, and no operator page was read. The agreement of MediaTek's file with Google, 49 of its 56 scopes with a Google rule and none opposite, is a word about the file. It excludes these networks: the 8 profiles here are its 7 scopes Google leaves unset and its 1 with no rule. 23 of the 98 bundles are Dish-shaped: GID profiles on 302-220 whose GIDs sit in Google's dish5gsa_us rule on 313-340 (Dish US 8, Dish 5G 6, Boost 2, unnamed 7). Their true came from the 2020 TELUS block and was never a word about Dish.
findings.effect: rtt_supported_bool (CarrierConfigManager.java:3418, default false at :12190). With true and ignore_rtt_mode_setting_bool at its default true (:11996), ImsManager.updateRttConfigValue provisions RTT on and keeps IMS turned on even when nothing else needs it (ImsManager.java:2756-2797, 1763-1785). ImsRegistrationTracker then adds TEXT beside each VOICE capability, using rtt_supported_while_roaming_bool when roaming (ImsRegistrationTracker.java:419-424, 585-598). AosHandleEmergencyMtc adds TEXT to the emergency registration whenever the key is true, with no roaming or network check (AosHandleEmergencyMtc.cpp:45-63). AosCondition.IsDeregRequiredForTty deregisters in TTY mode only when RTT is off, VoLTE TTY is off and the phone is combined-attached (AosCondition.cpp:998-1031). AosRegistration.UpdateNetworkFeatureRtt marks TEXT unavailable on a normal registration the network does not confirm (AosRegistration.cpp:1210-1245). A call type is cut down to the registered features (CallTypeUtil.cpp:24-66), and a voice call stays audio only (MtcMediaUtil.cpp:74-92, IdleState.cpp:550-552). Emergency TTY routing reads carrier_volte_tty_supported_bool, not this key (EmergencyCallDomainSelector.java:755-756, 1168-1169, 2045-2057). Telephony's own gate needs R.bool.config_support_rtt, which is false on 23.2 and on lineage-24.0 (config.xml:235, no overlay in the x1s device trees), so isRttSupported and isRttEnabled are false and the PhoneAccount has no RTT capability (PhoneInterfaceManager.java:7995-8035, TelecomAccountRegistry.java:1128-1154). Telecom still creates RTT streams for an emergency call when the calling app asks for RTT (CallsManager.java:2650-2662). ImsManager.java at android-17.0.0_r1 equals the tree. On a phone: admitted only for the most specific profile that sets the key, else the Google-lane value, else Android's default false (Serving.kt:405-440).
findings.risk: No harm was found. Served true, the emergency REGISTER gains TEXT with no network check, IMS stays on with VoLTE off and the native TTY deregistration stops. No source shows how these networks treat that tag from this stack, and no test can see it. The gain is small: the stock dialler cannot start RTT, since config_support_rtt is false. From holding, the phone reads Android's default false, what a Pixel reads with these SIMs. With RTT off and carrier_volte_tty_supported_bool false, a TTY user on a combined-attached SIM goes back to the native deregistration, as on any SIM with RTT off.

notes: Not admitted on this stack: these 37 profiles rest on one maker or one file, so the phone reads Android's default false on their 98 bundles. No harm was found, and nothing shows these networks lack RTT. The hold rests on missing basis, and it is no fact about the networks. A second source for a network releases it, and that means a Google entry or an operator statement read in full. A second file from the same maker, a regulator's rule or a file's average agreement does not. The 23 Dish-shaped bundles on 302-220 get no exception and no selector is added: Dish on 302-220 gets true only through a read of its own basis.
